nodes.label: Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit
nodes.summary_es: Crédito de impuestos que le devuelve dinero si pagó cuidado de niños o de un dependiente con discapacidad para poder trabajar o buscar trabajo.
nodes.summary_en: Tax credit that gives money back if you paid for child care or care of a disabled dependent so you could work or look for work.
nodes.who: To claim the federal Child Tax Credit, you need to meet all of these requirements: You (and your spouse if filing a joint return) have earned income; You paid for care so you could work (you must identify your care provider with their name, address, and tax ID or Social Security Number on your tax return); You're filing as single, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse, or married filing jointly; Who counts as a dependent? A child under age 13 who you claim as a dependent, or; Your spouse or dependent of any age who can't care for themselves due to a physical or mental disability and lives with you for more than half the year; If you qualify for the federal credit, you can also claim the New York State credit when you file your state taxes. The state credit works the same way as the federal credit. You can get an additional NYC credit if you meet all of these requirements: You lived in NYC for all or part of 2025.; You paid childcare expenses for at least one child under age four on December 31, 2025.; Your federal adjusted gross income was $30,000 or less.; You qualified for the New York State credit.

nodes.label: Extended Day/Year Infant and Toddler Programs
nodes.summary_es: Cuidado y educación temprana gratis o a bajo costo para niños de 6 semanas a 5 años, hasta 10 horas al día, todo el año.

nodes.label: Child Tax Credit (CTC)
nodes.summary_es: Créditos de impuestos federal y estatal de hasta $3,200 por niño menor de 4 años y hasta $2,700 por niño de 4 a 16. Se reclaman al declarar impuestos.
nodes.summary_en: Federal and Empire State tax credits worth up to $3,200 per child under 4 and up to $2,700 per child ages 4 to 16. Claim when you file taxes.
nodes.who: To claim the federal Child Tax Credit, you need to meet all of these requirements: Filing status Annual income limit Single, head of household, or qualifying surviving spouse Up to $200,000 Married filing jointly Up to $400,000 You must have: A child, stepchild, grandchild, foster child, adopted child, sibling, niece, or nephew under age 17; A Social Security Number (SSN) or Adoption Tax Identification Number (ATIN) for yourself and your dependent(s); Lived with your dependent(s) for more than half the year in the US; Claimed the dependent on your tax return (the dependent cannot provide more than half of their own financial support) ; Important: Only one parent can claim a child for the CTC. nodes.label: Disability Rent Increase Exemption (DRIE)

nodes.summary_en: Rent freeze for New Yorkers with disabilities who receive a qualifying disability benefit and live in certain apartments.
nodes.who: To qualify for DRIE, you'll need to meet basic requirements, live in certain types of apartments, and receive a qualifying disability benefit. nodes.label: Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
nodes.summary_es: Crédito de impuestos de hasta $11,000 para personas que trabajan tiempo completo, tiempo parcial o por cuenta propia.
nodes.summary_en: Tax credit worth up to $11,000 for people who work full time, part time, or are self-employed.
nodes.who: Income requirements for the federal EITC Your 2025 income must fall within these limits: Household type Annual income limit Married with qualifying children Up to $68,675 Married without qualifying children Up to $26,214 Single with qualifying children Up to $61,555 Single without qualifying children Up to $19,104 Other federal requirements You must have a valid Social Security number; Your investment income in 2025 must have been less than $11,950; You must be between 25 and 64 years old if you don't have dependents (can be your children, stepchildren, foster children, or grandchildren) ; You can claim the EITC if your dependent(s) lived with you for more than half the year and you were legally separated at the end of 2025 or lived apart from your spouse for the last six months of 2025; Requirements for state and city credits If you qualify for the federal EITC, you automatically qualify for New York State and City credits when you file your state taxes. Not sure if you qualify? Use the IRS calculator to check your eligibility.

nodes.label: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)
nodes.summary_es: Beneficios mensuales en una tarjeta EBT para comprar comida. Depende principalmente de los ingresos y el tamaño del hogar.
nodes.summary_en: Monthly benefits on an EBT card to buy groceries. Eligibility is based mainly on household income and size.
nodes.who: SNAP eligibility is primarily based on: How much money you earn; How many people are in your household

nodes.label: Comprehensive After School System of NYC (COMPASS NYC)
nodes.summary_es: Programas gratis después de la escuela con ayuda con tareas, deportes y artes para estudiantes de NYC de kínder a 12.º grado.
nodes.summary_en: Free after-school programs with homework help, sports, and arts for NYC students in kindergarten to 12th grade.
nodes.who: All NYC students in kindergarten to 12th grade are eligible to enroll in COMPASS programs. Each program may have different age and eligibility requirements.

nodes.label: Cash Assistance
nodes.summary_es: Ayuda en efectivo para pagar renta, servicios y otros gastos de emergencia. Los adultos que pueden trabajar deben trabajar, estudiar o capacitarse.

nodes.who: This program looks at several things to decide if you are eligible. Some of them include: how much money you earn; how much money you receive from benefits; how many people live in your house; resources like cash or a checking account

nodes.label: Qualified Health Plans (QHP)

nodes.who: You can enroll in a Qualified Health Plan if you: Live in New York State; Are a U.S. citizen or legally living in the U.S.; Do not qualify for Medicaid, the Essential Plan, or Child Health Plus

nodes.label: School Tax Relief Program (STAR)
nodes.summary_es: Pago anual del crédito STAR que ayuda a propietarios elegibles del estado de Nueva York a pagar impuestos sobre la propiedad.

nodes.label: Senior Citizen Homeowners' Exemption (SCHE)
nodes.summary_es: Impuestos sobre la propiedad más bajos para propietarios mayores con ingresos por debajo de un límite.
nodes.summary_en: Lower property taxes for senior homeowners whose income is under a set limit.
nodes.who: To be eligible for SCHE, you must meet these requirements: Own a one-, two-, or three-family home, condo, or coop apartment.; All owners of the property are 65 or older. However, if you own the property with a spouse or sibling, only one of you need to be 65 or older.; All owners must live on the property as the primary residence.; The combined income for all owners must be less than or equal to $58,399.; You must own the property for at least 12 consecutive months before the date of filing for the exemption. This is not a requirement if you got the exemption on a property that you owned before.

nodes.label: Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption (SCRIE)
nodes.summary_es: Congelación del alquiler para personas de 62 años o más que viven en ciertos apartamentos, para que puedan quedarse en su hogar.
nodes.summary_en: Rent freeze for seniors 62 and older who live in certain rentals, so they can stay in their homes.
nodes.who: To be eligible for SCRIE, you should be able to answer "yes" to all of these questions: Are you 62 or older?; Is your name on the lease (or the share certificate if you live in a Mitchell-Lama development)?; Is your combined household income $50,000 or less in a year?; Do you spend more than one-third of your monthly income on rent?; Do you live in NYC in one of these types of housing?a rent stabilized apartment; a rent controlled apartment; a rent regulated hotel or single room occupancy unit; a Mitchell-Lama development; a Limited Dividend Housing Company development; a Redevelopment Company development; a Housing Development Fund Company development

nodes.label: Beacon Programs
nodes.summary_es: Centros comunitarios en escuelas para jóvenes de 5 a 21 años.
nodes.summary_en: School-based community centers for young people ages 5 to 21.
nodes.who: Youth ages 5-21 who are enrolled in school can participate.; Beacon also offers adult programs for people who are over 21 years old.

nodes.label: NYC Free Tax Prep
nodes.summary_es: Preparación de impuestos gratis en más de 140 lugares de NYC, en persona, en línea o por teléfono.
nodes.summary_en: Free tax preparation at over 140 NYC locations, in person, online, or by phone.
nodes.who: For tax year 2025, youre eligible for NYC Free Tax Prep if you earned: $97,000 or less in 2025 and have qualifying children or dependents; $68,000 or less in 2025 and do not have qualifying children or dependents

nodes.label: CUNY Fatherhood Academy (CFA)
nodes.summary_es: Ayuda con educación, empleo y crianza para padres de 18 a 30 años.
nodes.summary_en: Education, job, and parenting help for fathers ages 18 to 30.
nodes.who: To be eligible for CUNY Fatherhood Academy, you should be able to answer yes to these questions. For the high school equivalency AND college prep track: Do you live in New York City?; Are you a father or an expecting father?; For the high school equivalency track only: Are you between 18 and 30 years old?; Can you commit to a 16-week program for three days a week?; For the college prep track only: Are you between 18 and 30 years old?; Do you have a high school diploma, HSE diploma, or GED?; Do you have less than 12 college credits?; Are you currently not enrolled in college?

nodes.label: Newborn Home Visiting Program (NHVP)
nodes.summary_es: Visitas gratis al hogar para padres primerizos con recién nacidos de hasta 3 meses: apoyo con lactancia, salud y seguridad.
nodes.summary_en: Free home visits for first-time parents of newborns up to 3 months old: breastfeeding, health, and safety support.
nodes.who: To be eligible for this program, you should be a first-time parent who lives in one of these neighborhoods. You may also be eligible if you are a parent with a baby less than 3 months old and who: lives in a NYCHA development in one of these neighborhoods.; currently gets help from the Administration for Children's Services (ACS).; lives in a Department of Homeless Services (DHS) shelter.

nodes.label: Children and Youth with Special Health Care Needs (CYSHCN)
nodes.summary_es: Ayuda para niños con condiciones médicas que necesitan servicios médicos especiales.
nodes.summary_en: Help for children with medical conditions that require special medical services.
nodes.who: Eligible children must: Be age 21 or younger; Live in New York City; Have been diagnosed with or may have a serious or chronic health condition, physical disability, or developmental or emotional/behavioral condition; Need extra health care and assistance

nodes.label: Outpatient Treatment Services
nodes.summary_es: Ayuda ambulatoria para jóvenes con problemas emocionales, de conducta o de salud mental.
nodes.summary_en: Outpatient help for young people with emotional, behavioral, and mental health challenges.
nodes.who: Clinic treatment is available for: Children from birth to age 18 (not all clinics accept children under 5 years old); Children with emotional, behavioral, or mental health challenges; Day treatment programs are available for: Children between the ages of 3 and 18 (there are two programs in NYC for children ages 3 - 5); Children with mental health disorders that interfere with school or social functions in a major way; Children who have serious difficulties in a regular classroom

nodes.label: Primary and Preventive Health Care
nodes.summary_es: Atención médica para niños y jóvenes en clínicas y centros de salud escolares, sin importar el estatus migratorio ni la capacidad de pago.
nodes.summary_en: Health care for children and youth at clinics and school-based health centers, regardless of immigration status or ability to pay.
nodes.who: All New York City youth are eligible for health care regardless of immigration status or whether they can pay; For primary care services, youth need to bring a parent or guardian for the first visit. They can get a form signed so they can come by themselves for future visits.

nodes.label: Living for the Young Family Through Education (LYFE)
nodes.summary_es: Educación temprana gratis para hijos de padres estudiantes, de 6 semanas a 4 años.
nodes.summary_en: Free early childhood education for children of student-parents, ages 6 weeks to 4 years.
nodes.who: You may be eligible for LYFE if you answer yes to the following questions: Are you enrolled in or eligible to enroll inan NYC Department of Education school or program?; Is your child between 6 weeks and 4 years old, and not age-eligible for Pre-K for All?

nodes.label: Family Resource Centers (FRC)
nodes.summary_es: Apoyo entre pares para padres e hijos con problemas emocionales, de conducta o de salud mental.
nodes.summary_en: Peer-led support for parents and children facing emotional, behavioral, or mental health challenges.
nodes.who: Parents or caregivers of a child 0 to 24 years old who is at risk of or currently experiences emotional, behavioral or mental health challenges.

nodes.label: Family Assessment Program (FAP)
nodes.summary_es: Ayuda para familias con problemas como un hijo que falta a la escuela o usa sustancias, sin ir a la corte. No necesita un caso abierto con ACS.
nodes.summary_en: Help for families with problems like a child skipping school or substance use, without involving the courts. No open ACS case needed.
nodes.who: Children up to 18 years old and their families who are struggling to relate to one another can get help.; Any family can get help from FAP; you do NOT need to have an open ACS case.

nodes.label: Cornerstone Programs
nodes.summary_es: Programas todo el año para jóvenes y adultos en centros comunitarios de vivienda pública de NYCHA.
nodes.summary_en: Year-round programs for youth and adults at NYCHA public housing community centers.
nodes.who: Cornerstone Programs are available to NYCHA residents who are Kindergarten-age or older.

nodes.label: The Early Intervention Program (EIP)
nodes.summary_es: Apoyo gratis para bebés y niños pequeños con discapacidades o retrasos en el desarrollo, y sus familias.
nodes.summary_en: Free support for infants and toddlers with disabilities or developmental delays, and their families.
nodes.who: To be eligible for EIP your child must: Live in New York City.; Be under the age of three (up to two years and 11 months).; Be evaluated (program staff will help you choose an evaluating agency).

nodes.label: Home Care Services Program (HCSP)
nodes.summary_es: Atención médica en el hogar para personas mayores y con discapacidad.
nodes.summary_en: Health care at home for seniors and people with disabilities.
nodes.who: Home care programs have different eligibility requirements, but they all require that you must be eligible for Medicaid.

nodes.label: NYCHA Public Housing
nodes.summary_es: Vivienda pública asequible para neoyorquinos de ingresos bajos y moderados. La renta depende de los ingresos de su familia.
nodes.summary_en: Affordable public housing for low- and moderate-income New Yorkers. Rent is based on your family's income.
nodes.who: To qualify for public housing, all of the following must be true: At least one person in your household is a U.S. citizen or has legal immigration status such as permanent resident (Green Card), refugee, or asylum status.; You're 18 or older, or you're an emancipated minor.; If you're applying with a spouse or domestic partner, they're also 18 or older, or an emancipated minor.; If you're applying for senior public housing, everyone in your household is 62 or older.; Your household qualifies as a family under NYCHA's rules. This includes two or more people related by blood, marriage, domestic partnership, adoption, guardianship, or court-awarded custodyand single people also qualify.; Your household income is at or below the income limits.; Family size Income in a year 1 $95,000 2 $108,600 3 $122,150 4 $135,700 5 $146,600 6 $157,450 7 $168,300 8 $179,150 9 $190,000 10 $200,850 11 $211,700 12 $222,550 13 $233,450 14 $244,300 15 $255,150

nodes.label: School-Age and Early Childhood Family and Community Engagement (FACE) Centers
nodes.summary_es: Información y recursos para jóvenes con discapacidades, de 0 a 21 años, y sus familias y cuidadores.
nodes.summary_en: Information and resources for young people with disabilities, ages 0 to 21, and their families and caregivers.
nodes.who: All NYC families who care for a child with disabilities are eligible to receive services for free. Trainings are open to everyone.

nodes.label: 3-K
nodes.summary_es: Educación gratis, de día completo y de alta calidad para niños de tres años en la Ciudad de Nueva York.
nodes.summary_en: Free, full-day, high-quality education for New York City three-year-olds.
nodes.who: All New York City families with children born in 2023 can apply for the upcoming school year. This includes children with disabilities or new English speakers. Children do not need to be toilet trained to attend 3-K.

nodes.label: Accelerated Study in Associate Programs (CUNY ASAP)
nodes.summary_es: Apoyo económico, académico y personal para que estudiantes de CUNY terminen su título asociado.
nodes.summary_en: Financial, academic, and personal support to help CUNY students finish an associate degree.
nodes.who: To be eligible for CUNY ASAP, you should: Apply and be accepted to a CUNY college that offers ASAP; Be a New York City resident or eligible for in-state tuition; Agree to enter into a full-time associate degree program in an ASAP-approved major; Be proficient in Math and/or English (reading and writing) ; Have no more than 15 college credits and a minimum GPA of 2.0.

nodes.label: CUNY Start
nodes.summary_es: Ayuda a estudiantes de CUNY a cumplir los estándares de competencia y prepararse para cursos universitarios.
nodes.summary_en: Helps CUNY students meet proficiency standards and prepare for college-level courses.
nodes.who: You might be eligible for CUNY Start/Math Start if you can answer yes to these questions: Have you earned a high school or high school equivalency diploma?; Have you completed all CUNY admissions requirements and accepted your offer to CUNY?; Could you benefit from extra support in English and/or math based on your proficiency index scores?; Are you able to commit to the program's academic schedule and its unique, student-centered instructional approach?; Specific colleges may have other eligibility criteria. Contact the CUNY Start program at your campus for more information.

nodes.label: Train & Earn
nodes.summary_es: Capacitación laboral, ayuda para conseguir empleo y preparación para el examen de equivalencia de secundaria para jóvenes que no trabajan ni estudian.
nodes.summary_en: Job training, employment help, and high school equivalency test prep for young people who are not working or in school.
nodes.who: To be eligible for Train & Earn, you need to meet all of these criteria: You live in NYC; You're 16-24 years old; You're registered for selective service, if you're an eligible male; You're not working; You're not attending school (and you haven't graduated high school or you don't have a high school equivalency diploma) OR you have a high school diploma or equivalency but are an English language learner or need to improve basic literary skills; You meet one of these requirements:You or someone in your household gets cash assistance or SNAP (food stamps); You are a homeless or runaway youth; You were in foster care or aged out of the foster care system; You are involved in the justice system; You have a disability; You are pregnant or a parent; You make less than the income limits in the chart below, and need more help to enter or finish an education program, or to get or hold a job. ; Household size Yearly income 1 $15,650 2 $21,150 3 $26,650 4 $32,150 5 $37,650 6 $43,150 7 $48,650 8 $54,150 For each additional person add $5,500

nodes.label: NYC Ladders for Leaders
nodes.summary_es: Pasantías pagadas de verano en empresas, organizaciones sin fines de lucro y agencias de NYC para estudiantes de secundaria y universidad.
nodes.summary_en: Paid summer internships at NYC companies, nonprofits, and government agencies for high school and college students.
nodes.who: You may be eligible if you can answer yes to these questions. Do you live in New York City?; Are you currently enrolled in high school or college?; Are you between 16 - 22 years old?; Do you have previous work experience (even as a volunteer)?; Do you have a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.00?; If you are under 18 years old, do you have your working papers?

nodes.label: Youth Action 50 (YA50)
nodes.summary_es: Permite a jóvenes ayudar a su comunidad participando en políticas, prácticas y abogacía para mejorar la ciudad.
nodes.summary_en: Lets young people help their communities by shaping policy, practice, and advocacy for citywide change.
nodes.who: Youth are eligible to apply for YA50 if they are: 14 - 21 years old; Enrolled in high school or an equivalency program

nodes.label: Jobs Plus
nodes.summary_es: Programa de empleo que ayuda a residentes de NYCHA a encontrar trabajo y ganar más.
nodes.summary_en: Employment program that helps NYCHA residents find jobs and increase their earnings.
nodes.who: NYCHA residents who are old enough to work and live in one of the 27 developments served can enroll in Jobs-Plus.

nodes.label: Career and Technical Education (CTE)
nodes.summary_es: Capacitación práctica para una carrera mientras termina la secundaria o la equivalencia de secundaria (HSE).
nodes.summary_en: Hands-on career training while finishing high school or a high school equivalency (HSE).
nodes.who: To be eligible to apply for a New York City public high school, you must be able to answer yes to these questions: Are you a New York City resident?; Are you currently an 8th-grade student or a first-time 9th-grade student?

nodes.label: Veterans Affairs Supported Housing (HUD-VASH)
nodes.summary_es: Ayuda para veteranos sin hogar y sus familias para encontrar y mantener vivienda permanente.
nodes.summary_en: Help for homeless veterans and their families to find and keep permanent housing.
nodes.who: You can qualify for HUD-VASH housing help if you: Served in the active military for any amount of time, and; Do not have a dishonorable discharge or a discharge from a general court-martial

nodes.label: Cooling Assistance Benefit
nodes.summary_es: Ayuda a hogares elegibles a comprar e instalar un aire acondicionado o ventilador para el calor.
nodes.summary_en: Helps eligible households buy and install an air conditioner or fan to stay cool during hot weather.
nodes.who: You may qualify by either: Meeting income limits: Your household's gross monthly income is at or below the limit for your household size (see table below), or ; Receiving other benefits: You currently receive one of the followingSNAP benefits (food stamps); Cash Assistance; Code A Supplemental Security Income (SSI Living Alone); A HEAP Regular Benefit over $21 this program year or equal to $21 if you live in government-subsidized housing (such as NYCHA or Section 8) with heat included in your rent; You or someone in your household must also: Have a documented medical condition worsened by extreme heat, be age 60 or older, or be under age 6; Be a U.S. citizen or qualified non-citizen (like a Green Card holder, refugee, asylee, or parolee) ; Not currently have a working air conditioner, or have one that is at least five years old; Not have received a HEAP-funded air conditioner within the past five years ; Household size Maximum household income for 2026 1 $3,473 2 $4,542 3 $5,611 4 $6,680 5 $7,749 6 $8,818 7 $9,018 8 $9,218 9 $9,419 10 $9,619 11 $9,820 12 $10,020 13 $10,221 Each additional person +$687

nodes.label: NYC Care
nodes.summary_es: Atención médica asequible en NYC Health + Hospitals para neoyorquinos que no tienen ni pueden pagar un seguro médico.
nodes.summary_en: Affordable health care at NYC Health + Hospitals for New Yorkers who don't have and can't afford health insurance.
nodes.who: You qualify for NYC Care if you: Live in NYC (any of the five boroughs); Don't have health insurance from your employer; Don't qualify for any health insurance plan available in New York State; Can't afford health insurance based on government guidelines

nodes.label: MOIA Immigration Legal Support Centers
nodes.summary_es: Evaluaciones legales de inmigración gratis en más de 20 centros. Abogados ayudan con ciudadanía, green card, DACA, TPS y más.
nodes.summary_en: Free immigration legal screenings at over 20 centers. Lawyers help with citizenship, green cards, DACA, TPS, and more.
nodes.who: If your annual household income is more than 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL), you may not be eligible to receive services from certain City-funded legal service providers. Household size Monthly household income (200% of FPL, 2026) 1 $2,660 2 $3,607 3 $4,553 4 $5,500 5 $6,447 6 $7,393 7 $8,340 8 $9,287 Each additional person +$947

nodes.label: Fair Fares NYC (FFNYC)
nodes.summary_es: Neoyorquinos de bajos ingresos de 18 a 64 años ahorran 50% en el metro, autobuses elegibles y viajes de Access-A-Ride.
nodes.summary_en: Low-income New Yorkers ages 18 to 64 save 50% on subway, eligible bus fares, and Access-A-Ride trips.
nodes.who: You may be eligible if you answer yes to these questions: Do you live in New York City?; Are you 18-64 years old?; Do you have a household income at or below these amounts?; Household size Yearly income 1 $23,475 2 $31,725 3 $39,975 4 $48,225 5 $56,475 6 $64,725 7 $72,975 8 $81,225 For each additional person +$8,250

nodes.label: We Speak NYC (WSNYC)
nodes.summary_es: Clases de inglés gratis, en línea y en persona, para personas de 16 años o más, con materiales sobre servicios de la Ciudad.
nodes.summary_en: Free English classes, online and in person, for learners 16 and older, with materials about City services.
nodes.who: Anyone is eligible to sign up for an online class. Classes and materials are created for intermediate English language learners ages 16 and above.

nodes.label: Homebase
nodes.summary_es: Apoyo para personas en riesgo de quedarse sin hogar, para evitar el albergue y mantener una vivienda estable.
nodes.summary_en: Support for people at risk of homelessness to stay out of shelter and keep stable housing.
nodes.who: You may be eligible for Homebase services if you: Live in one of the five boroughs of NYC; May be soon at risk of entering the NYC shelter system; Want to remain stably housed in your community; If you think you need Homebase services, contact a local office so they can review your specific situation and offer support. Even if you are not eligible, Homebase can help you find resources that might be helpful.

nodes.label: STEM Matters NYC
nodes.summary_es: Programas prácticos de ciencia y tecnología (STEM) para estudiantes de kínder a 12.º grado en vacaciones de primavera y verano.
nodes.summary_en: Hands-on STEM programs for K-12 students during spring break and summer.
nodes.who: Available to students entering grades 1 through 12 in NYC public and charter schools in September 2024.

nodes.label: COVID-19 Funeral Assistance
nodes.summary_es: Hasta $9,000 por cada funeral relacionado con COVID-19. Los ingresos no afectan la elegibilidad.
nodes.summary_en: Up to $9,000 for each funeral related to COVID-19. Income does not affect eligibility.
nodes.who: You may be eligible if: You are a U.S. citizen, noncitizen national, or qualified noncitizen.; You incurred COVID-19-related funeral expenses on or after January 20, 2020. ; The death was attributed to COVID-19, as noted on the death certificate.

nodes.label: Lifeline
nodes.summary_es: Un descuento mensual de hasta $9.25 en servicio de teléfono o internet para hogares elegibles.
nodes.summary_en: A monthly discount of up to $9.25 on phone or internet service for eligible households.
nodes.who: You're eligible for Lifeline if you answer yes to either question: Does someone in your household receive:Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP); Supplemental Security Income (SSI); Medicaid; Federal Public Housing Assistance (FPHA); Veterans Pension and Survivors Benefit; Does your household income meet these requirements?; Household size Maximum yearly income 1 $21,128 2 $28,553 3 $35,978 4 $43,403 5 $50,828 6 $58,253 7 $65,678 8 $73,103 For each additional person: +$7,425

nodes.label: Child Care Vouchers
nodes.summary_es: Vales que cubren la mayor parte o todo el costo del cuidado infantil en centros, proveedores en casa o con familiares y amigos.
nodes.summary_en: Vouchers that cover most or all child care costs at licensed centers, home-based providers, or with family and friends.
nodes.who: You may qualify if you get cash assistance or if your household income is below these amounts: Family size Monthly income 2 $6,601.24 3 $8,155.48 4 $9,707.70 5 $11,260.94 6 $12,814.18 7 $13,105.40 8 $13,396,64 9 $13,687.87 10 $13,979.10 11 $14,270.33 12 $14,561.56 13 $14,852.79 14 $15,144.03 15 $15,435.26 16 $15,726.49 17 $16,017.72 18 $16,308.95 19 $16,600.18 20 $16,891.41 Families who work 10+ hours per week must make at least minimum wage ($16.50/hour) to qualify for child care assistance. Each parent must have a qualifying reason for care: In school or job training; Looking for work; Unhoused; Receiving domestic violence services; Receiving treatment for substance misuse

nodes.label: NYC Financial Empowerment Centers
nodes.summary_es: Consejería financiera gratis e individual para manejar dinero, mejorar su crédito y hacer presupuesto, en su idioma. Para adultos que viven o trabajan en NYC.
nodes.summary_en: Free one-on-one financial counseling to manage money, improve credit, and budget, in your preferred language. For adults who live or work in NYC.
nodes.who: You qualify for free counseling if you're at least age 18 and live or work in NYC.

nodes.label: National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)
nodes.summary_es: Seguro contra inundaciones que cubre daños a su casa y sus pertenencias.
nodes.summary_en: Flood insurance that covers damage to your home and belongings.
nodes.who: Anyone in NYC can buy flood insurance.

nodes.label: Family Homelessness and Eviction Prevention Supplement (FHEPS)
nodes.summary_es: Paga parte o toda la renta para familias elegibles en riesgo de desalojo, en proceso de desalojo o en un albergue de HRA.
nodes.summary_en: Pays part or all of the rent for eligible families at risk of eviction, being evicted, or living in an HRA shelter.
nodes.who: Your family must have one of the following:A child under 18 years of age; A child under 19 years of age who is enrolled full-time in high school or a vocational or technical training program; A pregnant person; One of these must also apply to your family:Have an active Cash Assistance case; If you are in shelter, qualify for Cash Assistance when you leave shelter; Your family must also meet one of the following:You are in HRA shelter.; You are in DHS shelter and eligible for HRA shelter.; You are in DHS shelter and were evicted* in NYC sometime in the year before you entered shelter.; You are currently being evicted or were evicted* in NYC within the last 12 months.; *Evicted can mean: An eviction proceeding against you or the person on the lease for your home.; A foreclosure action for your building or home.; A City agency said that you must leave your building or home because of health or safety reasons.; A landlord has issued you a rent demand letter and threatened an eviction for non-payment of rent.

nodes.label: NYS Paid Family Leave (PFL)
nodes.summary_es: Hasta 12 semanas de licencia pagada, con protección del empleo, para cuidar a un bebé, a un familiar enfermo y otras situaciones.
nodes.summary_en: Up to 12 weeks of paid, job-protected time off to care for a new child, a sick family member, and other situations.
nodes.who: You may be able to take Paid Family Leave if you: Are a resident of New York State.; Work for a private employer in New York State or for a public employer who has opted in.Some workers aren't eligible for PFL Learn more about what kinds of workers are eligible.; If youre not sure if you're covered for PFL, speak to your employer. ; Meet the time-worked requirements before taking Paid Family Leave:Full-time employees who regularly work 20 or more hours/week can take PFL after working 26 consecutive weeks.; Part-time employees who regularly work less than 20 hours/week can take PFL after working 175 days. These days don't need to be consecutive.

nodes.label: Family Type Homes for Adults (FTHA)
nodes.summary_es: Vivienda con apoyo para adultos que no pueden vivir solos por edad avanzada, discapacidad del desarrollo o salud física o mental.
nodes.summary_en: Supportive housing for adults who cannot live alone due to old age, developmental disabilities, or physical or mental health.
nodes.who: You must meet these basic requirements: Be at least 18 years old ; Need help with daily living tasks (you can't live independently without support); Have a developmental disability, physical disability, cognitive impairment, or mental illness; If you have certain diagnoses, you also need to: Attend a day treatment program (if you've been diagnosed with a developmental disability or mental illness); Be at least five years clean or sober (if you have a history of substance abuse); You won't qualify for FTHAs if you: Are wheelchair-bound or bed-ridden; Have a history of substance abuse (unless you're five years clean or sober); Have difficulties following medication and treatment plans; Have a history of arson; Have a history of verbal or abusive behavior; Have been incarcerated

nodes.label: NYC Child Care Connect (NYC CCC)
nodes.summary_es: Herramienta en línea para buscar programas de cuidado infantil en su comunidad y mantenerse informado.
nodes.summary_en: Online tool to find child care programs in your community and stay informed about them.
nodes.who: Population served: Families with children, Pregnant & new parents

nodes.label: Center For NYC Neighborhoods (CNYCN)
nodes.summary_es: Ayuda para propietarios para evitar la ejecución hipotecaria, manejar pagos atrasados de hipoteca y prevenir estafas.
nodes.summary_en: Help for homeowners avoiding foreclosure, dealing with late mortgage payments, and preventing scams.
nodes.who: Population served: All New Yorkers,  regardless of immigration status, Homeowners

nodes.label: Emergency Assistance / One Shot Deal
nodes.summary_es: Ayuda de emergencia en efectivo para un gasto que no puede pagar por un imprevisto, por ejemplo si puede perder su vivienda.
nodes.summary_en: Emergency cash help for an expense you can't pay because of an unexpected event, such as when you might lose your housing.
nodes.who: Eligibility is determined on a case-by-case basis. Factors that may be considered include: income (earned and unearned); household size; the reason for the need, like as losing a job; available savings and resources; affordability of housing; disability; a future plan to pay the expense moving forward; citizenship or immigration status

nodes.label: Runaway And Homeless Youth Drop-In Centers
nodes.summary_es: Albergue de emergencia y servicios de apoyo para jóvenes de 14 a 24 años sin hogar.
nodes.summary_en: Emergency shelter and support services for young people ages 14 to 24 experiencing homelessness.
nodes.who: Population served: All New Yorkers,  regardless of immigration status

nodes.label: NYC NY Connects
nodes.summary_es: Ayuda gratis para personas mayores y con discapacidad para seguir viviendo de forma independiente en su hogar y comunidad.
nodes.summary_en: Free help for older adults and people with disabilities to stay independent at home and in their community.
nodes.who: NY Connects is available to children and adults of all ages, regardless of a disability diagnosis, income level, or insurance. NY Connects also serves: Caregivers of older adults and parents of children with a disability.; Professional service providers working with someone in need of long term services and supports.

nodes.label: Homeless Intake Shelters & Drop-In Centers
nodes.summary_es: Solicite albergue o ayuda para encontrar vivienda estable si no tiene hogar o está en crisis de vivienda. Hay intérpretes disponibles.
nodes.summary_en: Apply for shelter or get help finding stable housing if you are homeless or in a housing crisis. Interpreters are available.
nodes.who: Visit an intake center to apply for shelter and discuss your eligibility. Drop-in centers are open to everyone.

nodes.label: NYC Housing Connect
nodes.summary_es: Portal en línea para buscar y solicitar apartamentos y casas asequibles para alquilar o comprar en los cinco condados.
nodes.summary_en: Online portal to find and apply for affordable apartments and homes to rent or buy in all five boroughs.
nodes.who: Each lottery has different income requirements based on your household size. Check the requirements on NYC Housing Connect before you apply. Ready to Rent offers free one-on-one financial counseling and help with applications. Some lotteries give priority to NYC residents who have a disability, are seniors, or live in the same neighborhood.

nodes.label: HomeFirst Down Payment Assistance
nodes.summary_es: Hasta $100,000 para el pago inicial o los costos de cierre de una casa nueva.
nodes.summary_en: Up to $100,000 toward the down payment or closing costs on a new home.
nodes.who: You will need to meet these income requirements to qualify for a HomeFirst loan: Family Size Maximum Household Income (120% AMI) 1 $136,080 2 $155,520 3 $174,960 4 $194,400 5 $210,000 6 $225,600 7 $241,080 8 $256,680 You will also need to meet all these criteria: Be a first-time homebuyer. This means you cannot have owned a home three years before buying a home with a HomeFirst loan. ; Provide documents to verify household income eligibility. This includes tax returns, pay stubs, profit and loss statements, or other documents.; Complete a homebuyer education course taught by an HPD-approved counseling agency.; Pay some of the down payment or closing costs.; Get a mortgage from a bank whose loans are regulated by a federal or state agency.To get a mortgage, you will need:an employment record, and; enough financial resources and credit; Buy a 1-4 family home, cooperative, or condominium. This must be in the five boroughs of New York City; The purchase price must be within approved limits.; The home must pass a housing inspection that certifies that it is safe to live in.; Live in the home as your primary residence. Depending on the loan amount, you will need to live in the home for at least:10 years for loans less than or equal to $40,000; 15 years for loans greater than $40,000.

nodes.label: NYC Mitchell-Lama
nodes.summary_es: Viviendas de alquiler y cooperativas para familias de ingresos moderados y medios. Se solicita a la lista de espera de cada edificio; puede tardar años.

nodes.summary_en: For unemployed or underemployed New Yorkers 55 and older: volunteer 15+ hours a week and get job training and credentials.
nodes.who: You're eligible for Silver Corps if you: are at least 55 years of age; are an NYC resident; are currently unemployed or underemployed; commit to volunteering a minimum of 15 hours per week in a nonprofit or government agency; are willing to participate in skills training and specialized training and/or credentialing programs; have income at or below these levels to qualify for a volunteer stipend and travel reimbursement:; Household size Your income 1 $62,600 2 $84,600 3 $106,600 4 $128,600 5 $150,600 6 $172,600 7 $194,600 8 $216,600 For each additional person: Add $22,000

nodes.label: Medicaid
nodes.summary_es: Cobertura médica para visitas al médico y clínica, chequeos, vacunas y más para residentes de Nueva York que cumplen límites de ingresos. Inscripción todo el año.
nodes.summary_en: Health coverage for doctor and clinic visits, checkups, immunizations, and more for New York residents who meet income limits. Enroll any time.
nodes.who: You may qualify for Medicaid if you: Live in New York State; Are a U.S. citizen or meet immigration status requirements; Meet income limits for your age group and household size; Check your income limit: Children under age 1; Children ages 1-18; Ages 19-20 living with your parents; Pregnant people; Adults under age 65, caretakers, and parents; Adults ages 65 and older, people with a disability or visual impairment ; If your income is too high for Medicaid, you could still qualify through the Medicaid Excess Income Program.

nodes.label: Big Apple Connect
nodes.summary_es: Internet en casa y cable básico desde $0 al mes para residentes de desarrollos participantes de NYCHA, con Optimum o Spectrum.
nodes.summary_en: Home internet and basic cable for as low as $0 a month for residents of participating NYCHA developments, through Optimum or Spectrum.
nodes.who: You can enroll in Big Apple Connect if you live in any of these NYCHA developments .

nodes.summary_en: Discounted NYC Ferry fares for seniors 65+, people with disabilities, high school students, and Fair Fares NYC participants.
nodes.who: Get discounted one-way ferry tickets if you're: 65 or older; A person with a disability; A NYC high school student; A Fair Fares NYC participant

nodes.label: MTA Reduced-Fare Program
nodes.summary_es: Tarifas reducidas del MTA para personas de 65 años o más o con una discapacidad que califica.
nodes.summary_en: Reduced MTA fares for anyone 65 or older or with a qualifying disability.
nodes.who: You qualify if any of the following apply: Are 65 or older; Receive Medicare benefits for any reason other than age; Have a serious mental illness and receive Supplemental Security Income (SSI); Have blindness; Have deafness or hearing loss; Have an ambulatory, cognitive, or other physical disability

nodes.summary_es: Por ley del estado de Nueva York, los trabajadores tienen 20 horas de licencia prenatal pagada cada año.
nodes.summary_en: By New York State law, workers get 20 hours of paid prenatal leave every year.
nodes.who: See if you're eligible for Paid Prenatal Leave: Eligible employees Full- and part-time employees in the private sector; Employees of non-profit organizations; Not eligible Federal, state, or local government employees

nodes.label: Affordable Broadband Act (ABA)
nodes.summary_es: Internet en casa con descuento si recibe SNAP, Medicaid u otros beneficios.
nodes.summary_en: Discounted home internet if you receive SNAP, Medicaid, or other benefits.
nodes.who: You may qualify for low-cost home internet if someone in your household receives any of the following benefits: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program; Medicaid; Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption; Disability Rent Increase Exemption ; Affordability benefit from a utility, such as the Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP); Free or reduced-priced lunch through the National School Lunch Program; Not enrolled in any qualifying programs? You may still qualify based on household income. Contact your internet provider for income limits.

nodes.label: Summer EBT
nodes.summary_es: Niños elegibles de 6 a 16 años reciben $120 para comprar comida cuando no hay clases en el verano.
nodes.summary_en: Eligible kids ages 6 to 16 get $120 for groceries when school is out for the summer.
nodes.who: Most eligible kids between ages 6 to 16 are approved automatically. You do not need to apply if your child is enrolled in: SNAP (food stamps); Cash assistance; Medicaid; Free or reduced-price school meals; If you qualify automatically, youll get a letter in the mail. Not automatically approved? You can apply if both of the following are true: Your child attends a school in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP); Your household income is at or below the monthly limits; Household size Maximum monthly income for 2026 1 $2,461 2 $3,337 3 $4,212 4 $5,088 5 $5,964 6 $6,839 7 $7,715 8 $8,591 Each additional person +$876

nodes.label: Senator José Peralta NYS DREAM Act
nodes.summary_es: Estudiantes indocumentados y otros que terminaron la secundaria o el GED en Nueva York pueden recibir ayuda estatal para la universidad, como TAP y Excelsior. Se solicita una vez.
nodes.summary_en: Undocumented and other students who finished high school or a GED in New York can get state college aid like TAP and Excelsior. Apply once, any time.
nodes.who: Students who received their high school degree or GED in New York State and students receiving in-state tuition, including undocumented students. Accepted statuses: T visa holder; U visa holder; Temporary Protected Status (TPS); DACA recipient; pending lawful immigration status; U.S. citizens and permanent residents whose permanent home is outside NYS. Educational requirements: graduated from a NYS high school after attending for at least two years; or received a NYS high school equivalency diploma; or were charged in-state tuition at a SUNY or CUNY campus for reasons other than residency.

nodes.label: Students in Temporary Housing Transportation (McKinney-Vento)
nodes.summary_es: Estudiantes en vivienda temporal reciben transporte gratis a la escuela en autobús escolar o tarjeta OMNY. Padres de niños de 3-K a 12.º grado sin autobús también reciben OMNY.
nodes.summary_en: Students in temporary housing ride free to school by school bus or student OMNY card. Parents of 3-K to 12th graders without busing can get OMNY too.
nodes.who: Students in temporary housing under the McKinney-Vento Act: living doubled up with friends or relatives because they cannot find or afford housing; in a shelter or transitional shelter; a hotel/motel; a car, bus or train; a park or public place; or an abandoned building. Includes unaccompanied youth. Eligible for free transportation while homeless, through the end of the school year in which they become permanently housed, and for an additional year if entering the final grade in their school. Parents/guardians of students in temporary housing in 3-K to grade 12 who do not receive busing can get an OMNY card to accompany their child.

nodes.label: NYC Schools Account (NYCSA)
nodes.summary_es: Un solo acceso para ver calificaciones y exámenes de su hijo, actualizar contactos de emergencia, obtener formularios escolares y reportar acoso escolar.
nodes.summary_en: One login to see your child's grades and test scores, update emergency contacts, get school forms, and report bullying.
nodes.who: Parents and guardians of NYC public school students. Starting later in the 2026-2027 school year, all parents identified in NYCPS systems as the child's parent/guardian can open an account, regardless of custodial status.

nodes.label: Tandas (rotating savings groups) explained
nodes.summary_es: Una tanda es un grupo informal de ahorro: cada miembro aporta a un fondo común y lo recibe por turno. Sin intereses, pero puede ser riesgosa.
nodes.summary_en: A tanda is an informal savings group: members pay into a shared fund and each receives it in turn. No interest, but informal savings can be risky.
nodes.who: Informal groups. The NYC Department of Consumer Affairs study describes tandas as a common savings tool among Mexican immigrants in New York City, ranging from about 10 family members and close friends to a 50-person group run by an organizer.

nodes.label: Lending Circles (credit-building zero-interest loans)
nodes.summary_es: Préstamos sin interés de $300 a $2,400 en grupos de 6 a 12 personas. Los pagos se reportan a las tres agencias de crédito principales para crear historial.
nodes.summary_en: Zero-interest loans of $300 to $2,400 shared by groups of 6 to 12 people. Payments are reported to all three major credit bureaus to build credit.
